title: Native Galaxy scale visual response product feel

scope.subject: Tune the existing pinned MIT YEIS Galaxy scale bridge so the product coordinate directly scrubs a modest stateless visual response curve with earlier perceptible target growth, exact endpoints, immediate reversal, and no time-driven continuation

research_summary: Personal Universe already feeds one product-owned continuous scale coordinate into the retained native YEIS CameraController trajectory. The remaining Galaxy feel gap is perceptual: early raw trajectory progress can read as dead across astronomical distances. Reuse the existing YEIS gotoPoint/autopilot-progress bridge and apply only a small monotonic stateless progress remap before setAutopilotProgress. Product coordinate, target identity, endpoint semantics, reference-frame handling, manual takeover, and wheel ownership remain unchanged. No second camera, tween, inertia loop, or autonomous progress is added.

sources.finding: Pinned MIT YEIS remains the approved native Galaxy renderer and CameraController trajectory authority; product scale should scrub that retained path rather than create another camera or path.

The close-world camera executor is separate and its wheel action remains disabled; Galaxy response tuning must stay inside the existing native bridge and not introduce another wheel or damping authority.

search_ladder.conclusion: Retain the existing YEIS-native Galaxy scale path and tune only how the already-owned product coordinate scrubs it.
Keep the current R3F host and imperative native bridge; no new animation framework is needed.
Reuse CameraController gotoPoint plus setAutopilotProgress as the trajectory executor and remap only the supplied progress.
Do not re-enable camera-controls wheel physics or add damping; it remains the close-world executor only.

candidates.name: Stateless visual response over retained YEIS native progress
candidates.license: MIT pinned upstream plus project bridge
candidates.reason: Improves early Galaxy perceptibility while preserving the existing physical path, target, endpoint, reversal, reference frame, and single input authority.

candidates.name: Project-owned Galaxy camera tween
candidates.reason: Would duplicate the native path and create stale time-driven motion after delivered input ends.

coverage_matrix.capability: Early Galaxy input produces perceptible motion without changing product coordinate semantics
coverage_matrix.decision: Apply a monotonic stateless visual progress function immediately before setAutopilotProgress.

coverage_matrix.capability: Reverse input retraces the same native path immediately
coverage_matrix.decision: The remap depends only on the current product coordinate, so no old-direction state can survive a sign change.

decision.rationale: Reuse the current native bridge and pinned YEIS trajectory executor. Only transform the scalar progress passed to the retained setAutopilotProgress call; all input, target, cancellation, and endpoint authority stays where it is.
decision.fallback: If visual evidence shows the curve is too strong, reduce its easing weight while preserving monotonicity and non-zero endpoint slope; never replace it with elapsed-time tweening or project-owned inertia.
